# Memrain — llms.txt

> Map of where things live, for AI agents that just cloned the repo.
> Read CLAUDE.md first (it's loaded automatically), this file second.

## What this repo is

Memrain Lite: self-hosted long-term memory for one person's AI agents,
reached over MCP only.
- **Memrain** — knowledge brain (Bun + Postgres + pgvector). Pages with
  version history, links and tags, and hybrid search (a keyword arm and a
  vector arm fused with RRF) behind 29 MCP tools, all declared in
  `deploy/memrain/src/mcp/operations.ts`. Retrieval only: the one model call
  is Bedrock Titan v2 embeddings (none with `MEMRAIN_KEYWORD_ONLY=1`); answers
  are the MCP client's job. Safety checks on every write: secret scan with
  sealed originals, quarantine, write gate, owner-only sources. One hourly
  in-process housekeeping pass (purge, mirrors, embed gaps, token sweep,
  spend holds, retention); no worker, no daemons. PGLite is the local and
  dev engine.
- **cloudflared** — public HTTPS ingress for the MCP server
  (`brain.<domain>/mcp`) so MCP clients (Claude Code, claude.ai, GitHub Copilot, Codex,
  ChatGPT, …) connect.
  `ingress_mode = "caddy"` swaps it for a Caddy + Let's Encrypt sidecar
  on a public IP instead (see `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).

Both run as Docker Compose services on a single `t4g.medium` EC2.

## How callers authenticate

- **Personal access token** — `memrain auth create <name> --source <src>`, sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Bound to one source; `read,write` by default.
- **OAuth 2.1 client** — `memrain auth register-client …`. Memrain is its own
  authorization server (`/authorize`, `/token`, RFC 8414/9728 discovery).
  Browser connectors (claude.ai, ChatGPT) and CLI sign-ins use the
  authorization-code flow, approved by the owner in the admin panel. Dynamic
  Client Registration is off by default.
- **Static public bearer** — `<prefix>/memrain-public-bearer`, permanent, no
  tenant, public read subset only. Not for agents you trust with writes; hand
  out PATs or clients.

The owner signs in separately to the admin panel (`/admin`, passkeys). A
credential bound to a member other than the brain's owner, or carrying a
trust floor (`min_trust`), is refused with `credential_unsupported`.

`whoami` shows what a credential carries. Per-client guides: `docs/clients/`.

## Source code map

```
deploy/
├── docker-compose.yml           orchestrator (memrain + cloudflared + internal net)
├── memrain/                       knowledge brain
│   ├── Dockerfile               oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine
│   ├── package.json             pinned deps incl. yaml + chokidar + AWS SDK Bedrock + postgres
│   ├── memrain.yml.example        declarative runtime config overlay
│   ├── templates/               SOUL/USER/ACCESS_POLICY/HEARTBEAT.md.template (seeded by init)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── cli.ts               argparse + subcommand dispatch
│   │   ├── commands/            one file per subcommand (serve, import, reindex,
│   │   │                        doctor, auth, transcripts, write-gate, …).
│   │   │                        `bun run src/cli.ts --help` is the live list.
│   │   ├── http/                /health, /mcp, OAuth discovery + /authorize +
│   │   │                        /token, /admin
│   │   ├── mcp/                 JSON-RPC transport, tool dispatch, rate limiter
│   │   └── core/
│   │       ├── engine/          adapter pattern (interface, pglite, postgres, factory)
│   │       ├── search/          keyword + vector arms, fusion, filters
│   │       ├── housekeeping.ts  the hourly upkeep pass
│   │       ├── budget.ts        spend ledger and daily caps
│   │       ├── secret-store.ts, vault.ts   sealed originals of redacted secrets
│   │       ├── write-gate*.ts, quarantine.ts
│   │       └── migrations/      numbered SQL migrations (1-196, frozen)
│   ├── admin/                   admin panel front end (Vite)
│   └── docs/                    subsystem deep-dive (README, ARCHITECTURE, API, OPERATIONS)
├── cloudflared/                 public ingress sidecar (upstream image, no Dockerfile)
│   └── docs/
├── secrets/                     AWS Secrets Manager fetch
│   ├── fetch-secrets.sh         reads <secrets_prefix>/* into deploy/.secrets/
│   └── README.md
└── systemd/                     optional bearer-rotation unit; bootstrap does not install it

plugins/memrain/                 Claude Code + Codex plugin: MCP config and three skills

scripts/
├── audit.sh                     PII gate
├── init.sh                      interactive bootstrap (.env, tfvars, backend.hcl)
├── lib/
│   ├── pii-patterns.txt         audit input
│   └── pii-allowlist.txt        files exempt from audit
├── bootstrap.sh                 EC2 first-boot — runs from cloud-init user_data
└── rotate-memrain-public-bearer.sh   bearer rotation for the optional timer (not installed)

terraform/
├── main.tf                      providers + partial backend
├── variables.tf                 all input vars
├── *.tf                         per-resource files
├── terraform.tfvars.example     schema doc (real tfvars is gitignored)
├── backend.hcl.example          schema doc (real backend.hcl is gitignored)
└── user_data.sh.tftpl           cloud-init user_data template

tests/
├── audit.test.sh, init.test.sh  bash unit tests
└── test_*.py                    pytest suites (memrain skeleton, dockerfiles, etc.)

Makefile                         orchestration entry points
```

## Conventions you'll want to know

- Every secret is namespaced by `var.secrets_prefix` (default
  `memrain`, override via `scripts/init.sh` for fresh installs).
- The `.env` at repo root is the runtime contract — it's rendered by
  `scripts/init.sh` (local) or `scripts/bootstrap.sh` (on EC2).
- `make audit` reads `scripts/lib/pii-patterns.txt` and fails on any
  maintainer-private identifier — used as a pre-publish gate.
- AI agents working on this repo MUST honor `CLAUDE.md` — no commits
  without explicit ask, no destructive terraform without showing plan
  first, no unrequested infrastructure additions.

## Where to start when implementing a change

1. Skim `ARCHITECTURE.md` to place the change in the topology.
2. Find the closest existing pattern via grep — `secrets_prefix`,
   `dynamic "egress"`, `${EFS_MOUNT}`, etc. — match it.
3. Add tests before code: bash units in `tests/*.test.sh`, pytest in
   `tests/test_*.py`.
4. Update `CHANGELOG.md`, `TODO.md`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` in the same
   commit if behavior or topology changed.
5. `make audit && make test && terraform validate` before opening a PR.
